title: Modelling forests as social-ecological systems: A systematic comparison of agent-based approaches

key_points.claim: Review of 31 existing ABMs applied to managed forests using a social-ecological systems framework.
key_points.evidence_quote: we review the functionality of 31 existing agent-based models applied to managed forests

key_points.claim: Some models include advanced cognitive and emotional agent decision-making.
key_points.evidence_quote: Several applications include advanced cognitive and emotional decision-making

key_points.claim: Many models lack direct interactions and dynamic social/ecological processes.
key_points.evidence_quote: far from all demonstrate representation of key elements in a social-ecological system like direct interactions, and dynamic representations of social and ecological processes

key_points.claim: ABMs judged adequately complex for both social and ecological subsystems.
key_points.evidence_quote: agent-based approaches are adequately complex for simulating both social and ecological subsystems

key_points.claim: Three development avenues: calibration/validation standards; agent learning, adaptive governance, feedback loops; coupling to ecological models.
key_points.evidence_quote: robust methodological standards for calibration and validation of agent-based approaches; ii) modelling of agent learning, adaptive governance and feedback loops; iii) coupling to ecological models

reliability_notes: Abstract only (full text not retrieved). Peer-reviewed review article; domain-specific (forest social-ecological systems), not general artificial societies.
